title: Introduction to Laboratory Chemistry - Chemistry - Acid–Base Titration Techniques
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Before filling a buret with the titrant solution, it should be rinsed with distilled water and then rinsed with:
options: A small portion of the titrant solution.
questions.explain: Rinsing with the **titrant solution** ensures that any remaining water droplets inside the buret do not dilute the concentration of the titrant being used for the experiment.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: During an acid-base titration using phenolphthalein indicator, how is the endpoint visually identified?
options: When the solution turns from pink to colorless and stays colorless.
When a faint pink color persists for at least 30 seconds.
When the solution turns a deep, dark purple.
When a precipitate forms at the bottom of the flask.
questions.explain: The endpoint with phenolphthalein (titrating acid with base) is reached when the first trace of a **faint pink color persists** (usually for 30 seconds) in the swirling solution. A dark purple indicates the endpoint has been overshot.
